paras: The alleged whipping of Champion Jones was a reported flogging of a Black prisoner by masked white men near Pamplico, South Carolina, on the night of July 31, 1920, as a constable was driving him to the Florence county jail. The claim, made by the prisoner, was contradicted by a physician who found no whipping marks and by the constable, who said he drove off the men.

The prisoner, named 'Champion Jones' in one reading of the text and 'Hampton Jones' in another, was charged with assault and battery with intent to kill for cutting another Black man, not seriously, at a frolic at Pamplico that Saturday night. According to the report, he resisted arrest until a white man came to the officer's aid, and the officer used his club.

Constable Rose of Pamplico and a driver took the prisoner to Florence by car that night, reaching the county jail early Sunday morning. Jones said that in a swamp near Pamplico six or eight masked white men, whom he could not identify, stopped the car, took him from the protesting constable and severely whipped him in the woods.

After he reached the jail, a Florence physician examined him and found no signs of a whipping, the only wound being a severe cut in his head. The report attributed that cut to the arresting officer's club. Constable Rose stated that several men did try to stop the car in the swamp, but he shoved them off, sped away and landed his prisoner safely in jail. He said he took the men to be Black friends of the prisoner trying to free him.
No arrests of the men and no further inquiry appear in the coverage.

The only report found is a Florence dispatch of August 2, run by the Kingstree County Record on August 5 as 'Tells Strange Story / Negro Says He Was Whipped on Way to Jail.' The paper presented the whipping only as what 'the negro claims' and closed with the physician's finding and the constable's version. No coverage of the episode was found in the Black press.

accounts.label: Physician's examination
accounts.gist: A Florence physician found no signs of a whipping, only a severe cut in the head.

accounts.label: Constable's account
accounts.gist: Several men tried to stop the car in the swamp, but he shoved them off, sped away and brought the prisoner safely to jail; he took them to be Black friends of the prisoner trying to free him. The head cut came from his club when the prisoner resisted arrest.

framing.detail: The County Record headlined it 'Tells Strange Story', reported the whipping only as what the 'negro claims', and gave the last word to the physician and the constable, whose accounts discredit it.
